dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: Nam, I invited Ploy to my party, and she said "maybe." Is she coming or not?
dialogue.reading: ˈnɑːm, aɪ ɪnˈvaɪtɪd ˈplɔɪ tə maɪ ˈpɑːrti, ənd ʃiː ˈsɛd ˈmeɪbi. ɪz ʃiː ˈkʌmɪŋ ɔːr ˈnɑːt?

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Probably not. Thais tend to avoid saying no directly.
dialogue.reading: ˈprɑːbəbli ˈnɑːt. ˈtaɪz ˈtɛnd tu əˈvɔɪd ˈseɪɪŋ ˈnoʊ dəˈrɛktli.

dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: Why? In Canada, people tend to be more direct.
dialogue.reading: ˈwaɪ? ɪn ˈkænədə, ˈpiːpəl ˈtɛnd tə bi ˈmɔːr dəˈrɛkt.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: We don't like conflict. Saying no can make the other person feel bad.
dialogue.reading: wiː ˈdoʊnt ˈlaɪk ˈkɑːnflɪkt. ˈseɪɪŋ ˈnoʊ kən ˈmeɪk ði ˈʌðər ˈpɜːrsən ˈfiːl ˈbæd.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Yes. We tend to be indirect, so everyone can save face.
dialogue.reading: ˈjɛs. wiː ˈtɛnd tə bi ˌɪndəˈrɛkt, soʊ ˈɛvriwʌn kən ˈseɪv ˈfeɪs.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: It means you don't make someone feel embarrassed in front of other people.
dialogue.reading: ɪt ˈmiːnz juː ˈdoʊnt ˈmeɪk ˈsʌmwʌn ˈfiːl ɪmˈbærəst ɪn ˈfrʌnt əv ˈʌðər ˈpiːpəl.

dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: That's kind. But it's hard for me to understand.
dialogue.reading: ðæts ˈkaɪnd. bʌt ɪts ˈhɑːrd fər miː tu ˌʌndərˈstænd.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: You'll learn. And if you're not sure, just ask me!
dialogue.reading: juːl ˈlɜːrn. ənd ɪf jʊr ˈnɑːt ˈʃʊr, ˈdʒʌst ˈæsk miː!

dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: OK. Then is Ploy coming to my party or not?
dialogue.reading: oʊˈkeɪ. ˈðɛn ɪz ˈplɔɪ ˈkʌmɪŋ tə maɪ ˈpɑːrti ɔːr ˈnɑːt?
